$comment: Agent health. Loop counters never reset on reassignment. A reviewer returning REVISE has succeeded, not failed. Metrics exist for improvement, not ranking. retention.* records the CS-10 four-part test; a verdict here is a recommendation transcribed from Agent Operations, not a self-report. updatedAt is transcription time, not an invocation timestamp. attemptCount counts task dispatches only; a returned sprint-discussion contribution is recorded in invocationEvidence and does not increment it. lastError null means no failure was found, never an unread or unreadable record.

retentionPolicy.rule: Retain on any one leg. Merge only where artefact AND boundary AND decision are all duplicated. Never invoked is not grounds for removal.
retentionPolicy.criterion3Note: Zero agents merged or removed, correctly on the evidence. The criterion's intent is met by justification, not by action. Do not record as satisfied.

policyDefects.$comment: Defects found by Agent Operations while applying the CS-10 retention test. Items in .github/agents/ are OPERATOR-ACTION-REQUIRED: the Orchestrator deliberately does not edit agent definitions, because every permission guarantee in this system rests on agent tool-grants being operator-owned.

operatorActionRequired.finding: The activation-policy table is duplicated here and in .ai/AGENT-SETUP.md (lines 167-176) and the two CONTRADICT. Orchestrator copy line 72 says system redesign => "all"; AGENT-SETUP says "Orchestrator selects distinct specialists from the matrix; not all by default". AGENT-SETUP own retention rule says "Activate per task - never run all agents". The Orchestrator reads its own file, so the contradicting copy is the one that will be obeyed.
operatorActionRequired.fix: Delete the duplicate table from careerscope-orchestrator.agent.md and replace it with a pointer to .ai/AGENT-SETUP.md.

operatorActionRequired.finding: Says "Invoking all ten agents for a CSS fix" - the roster is 24.

Makes Product Architect and System Designer mutual fallbacks, while .ai/AGENT-SETUP.md lines 96-99 defends them as NOT duplicates. A role that can substitute for another is being treated as interchangeable with it. Both cannot be true.
operatorActionRequired.fix: Either drop the mutual fallback or drop the not-duplicates defence; this is the strongest available argument for merging overlap pair O-1.

operatorActionRequired.finding: Independent Reviewer falls back to Final Auditor. The Final Auditor is given no fallback precisely because it is the last independent check; spending it mid-loop leaves nothing fresh for FINAL_AUDIT.
operatorActionRequired.fix: Make a failed Independent Reviewer fall back to Code Quality + Security in combination, or to BLOCKED - never to the Final Auditor.

operatorActionRequired.finding: Says "Nine roles were added beyond the original eleven" = 20, not the 24 rows immediately above.
Says "Five roles were added"; contradicts AGENT-SETUP "nine" for the same event.

resolvedByOrchestrator.finding: The activation policy covered only 11 of 24 agents; 13 appeared in no row, including the Independent Reviewer - by the evidence the most-invoked specialist.

Seven change classes had no row at all: documentation-only, design-system/token, release cut or deploy execution, git/tag/commit, new skill/extension/MCP server, agent failure or blocked loop, backlog intake/feature proposal.
The "Copy or CSS" row omitted Visual Designer, which owns tokens and global stylesheets and was the agent actually dispatched for the real 2026-09-23 CSS/token change.
The "New dependency" row routed past both supply-chain reviewers (Security, Skills Curator).
.ai/LOOP-STATE.json records 18 of 24 agents WAITING while review.txt 2026-09-20 records contributions returned from all 24. Both true under different senses of "ran".
resolvedByOrchestrator.status: DISCLOSED 2026-09-24 via the invocationEvidence field on every agent record, which distinguishes task-dispatch from discussion-contribution from none. Only task-dispatch is retention evidence.
